2× Type-C 6-pin Female VERTICAL PCB-mount (8.83 × 8.83 mm) on a 30 × 20 mm perfboard scrap, 16 mm centre-to-centre. Openings face OUT of the page,
2× Type-C 6-pin Female VERTICAL PCB-mount (8.83 × 8.83 mm) on a 30 × 20 mm perfboard scrap, 16 mm centre-to-centre. Openings face OUT of the page,
through the two wall apertures at 180°. The board mounts copper-side-in on 4× Ø5 printed posts, M2 self-tap.
through the two wall apertures at 180°. The board mounts copper-side-in on 4× Ø5 printed posts, M2 self-tap.
THE BOARD CARRIES NO NETS. It is a mechanical bulkhead, not a circuit — all twelve conductors run point-to-point from a jack leg to the far end.
THE BOARD CARRIES NO NETS. It is a mechanical bulkhead, not a circuit — all twelve conductors run point-to-point from a jack leg to the far end.
Nothing to trace, bus or jumper. That is also why a pitch mismatch is survivable (Path B, below) rather than a failure.
Nothing to trace, bus or jumper. That is also why a pitch mismatch is survivable (Path B, below) rather than a failure.
→ PD trigger module's own USB-C · ~40 mm

VBUS + GND carry the full pack charge current — 28 AWG is ~1.4 A and UNDERSIZED.

carrier mount — anchor by the SHIELD legs (or VHB/epoxy the body), then solder flying leads straight to the 6 signal legs
carrier mount — anchor by the SHIELD legs (or VHB/epoxy the body), then solder flying leads straight to the 6 signal legs
Electrically identical — there were never any nets on this board. Decide per jack, note which you used, and do not fight a mismatch.
Electrically identical — there were never any nets on this board. Decide per jack, note which you used, and do not fight a mismatch.
Order — both jacks first, board bare and flat
Order — both jacks first, board bare and flat
1. SHIELD legs. Medium chisel, 350 °C, be generous. Structural joint.
1. SHIELD legs. Medium chisel, 350 °C, be generous. Structural joint.
Check the body sits square and the opening is perpendicular to the board.
Check the body sits square and the opening is perpendicular to the board.
2. The 6 signal legs. Fine conical, 340–350 °C, 0.5 mm solder, flux dot first.
2. The 6 signal legs. Fine conical, 340–350 °C, 0.5 mm solder, flux dot first.
Minimal solder — a bridge here is invisible until the port misbehaves.
Minimal solder — a bridge here is invisible until the port misbehaves.
3. Wires LAST. They get in the way and act as heat sinks.
3. Wires LAST. They get in the way and act as heat sinks.
⚠ ~2 s per leg, then move on.
⚠ ~2 s per leg, then move on.
USB-C jacks have plastic between the contacts that deforms and lets pins
USB-C jacks have plastic between the contacts that deforms and lets pins
tilt. If a leg won’t wet, add flux and come back after it cools.
tilt. If a leg won’t wet, add flux and come back after it cools.
Pre-tin the leg AND the wire end separately — it is a butt joint with no hole

to hold anything, so both sides must already be wetted.
to hold anything, so both sides must already be wetted.
Strip ~2 mm, heat-shrink on before you solder.
Strip ~2 mm, heat-shrink on before you solder.
Strain-relieve at the BOARD, not at the leg — a pull at the leg peels the pad.
Strain-relieve at the BOARD, not at the leg — a pull at the leg peels the pad.
Tie each jack’s shield to that jack’s GND lead; a floating shell just radiates.
Tie each jack’s shield to that jack’s GND lead; a floating shell just radiates.
